records.name: mini-SWE-agent

features_notes.durable_resume: Per-step JSON trajectories; no transactional scheduler or effect replay established.
features_notes.os_sandbox: Optional Docker environment; local environment executes on host and Docker defaults do not disable networking.
features_notes.approvals: Interactive subclass confirms actions; default agent does not.
features_notes.compaction: Absent from the inspected default loop.
features_notes.subagents: Absent from the inspected default loop.

dims.loop: Small query/action/environment loop; sequential actions, pre-request limits, exit-role termination.
dims.providers: Model protocol with LiteLLM and text/native action normalization.
dims.tools: Environment executes normalized action dictionaries; model adapter renders observations.
dims.context: Explicit message list and prompt templates; no default summarization.
dims.state: Finally-save trajectory JSON after steps; saved history is not effect replay.
dims.safety: Optional container relocation and interactive confirmation are separate choices.
dims.extensibility: Replace model/environment protocols or subclass the small agent.
dims.multi_agent: Default loop has no delegation or workflow scheduler.
dims.surfaces: Python library, interactive CLI and benchmark/headless runners.
dims.observability: Cost/call counts, serialized trajectories, rich/logging output.

records.one_liner: A small inspectable loop whose environment seam makes it useful for experiments and benchmark runners.
key_insights: A small model/environment protocol boundary keeps the default sequential loop easy to replace.
Per-step trajectory saves preserve history without providing transactional effect replay.
Interactive confirmation and Docker execution are optional, independent policies.

records.name: Aider
records.version: 0.86.3.dev source fallback; generated build version may override

features_notes.in_process_sdk: Importable Coder internals, not an independently stabilized generic harness API.
features_notes.durable_resume: Chat-history restoration and Git edits/commits; no inspected transactional replay engine.
features_notes.os_sandbox: Inspected editor and shell paths execute in the host environment.
features_notes.subagents: Architect-to-editor handoff is sequential; not a general supervisor.
features_notes.approvals: Edit and shell confirmation policies are configurable.

dims.loop: Coder loop applies edit-format responses and reflects parse/lint/test failures into subsequent requests.
dims.providers: LiteLLM model policy includes weak/editor models, edit format and token budget.
dims.tools: Repository editing, shell and Git operations sit inside coder subclasses.
dims.context: Weighted PageRank repository map plus file content and recursive history summarization.
dims.state: Chat history and Git track work; recovery does not provide durable side-effect replay.
dims.safety: Confirmation gates before edits/commands; no inspected OS isolation.
dims.extensibility: Subclass edit formats and configure models/context/I/O.
dims.multi_agent: Architect plans then a separate editor coder applies; history transfer is controlled.
dims.surfaces: Interactive CLI and importable Python internals.
dims.observability: Usage/cost output, chat histories, Git commits and diagnostic reflection.

records.one_liner: A repository editing product with strong code-context selection and repair loops, but limited generic runtime separation.
key_insights: Repository-map ranking and edit-format reflection are central to its coding workflow.
Importable coder internals are tightly coupled to repository, Git and interactive product policies.
Chat restoration and Git commits do not provide a durable workflow scheduler.

checks: Mini version module and trajectory schema distinguished
Mini sequential actions, finally-save and pre-call cost boundary inspected
Docker configuration and interactive approval defaults checked separately
Aider repository-map graph, edit reflection, summarization and Git/approval paths inspected
verification.limits: Pinned files and cited line ranges reviewed; no provider calls, package installs, runtime tests, security penetration tests or crash-injection experiments were performed.
